title: Mixing Blocking Synchronous and Non-Blocking Async Methods in a Single Trait
pattern: A single trait or interface defines a mixture of asynchronous, non-blocking methods and synchronous, blocking methods.
why_bad: Calling blocking operations inside an async executor starves the thread pool, causing massive latency spikes and deadlocks. It violates the operational consistency model of async systems.
detection: traits with a mix of `async fn` and normal `fn` returning database/network IO handles.
counterexample: Interface definitions for libraries explicitly bridging sync-async boundaries with separate, well-documented runtimes. Marked `Context-dependent`.
fix: Keep traits strictly async-only, or sync-only, using separate adapters for thread offloading.
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (2013), p. 308-309.
